A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Reward Models Inherit Value Biases from Pretraining. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–I are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original reward-model value analyses, controlled reward-model training experiments, and an experiment validating implicit reward measures in Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical investigations, including training-data ablations and the Qwen experiments, with revised numerical results.

M1.justification: Exhaustive token search, psycholinguistic value analysis, the mixture-weighted log-ratio (MWLR) score, and the reward-model training procedure are retained. The PDFs document no new algorithmic component or changed objective.

E1.justification: Both versions use the Big Two and MFD2 corpora, the same 54 prompts, Skywork and Unified Feedback data, and the authority-word validation task. The Qwen extension already appears in v1. Revised dataset quantities do not introduce new task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: The ten RewardBench models in Appendix A, the 21 Gemma–Llama comparisons, the GRM comparisons in Figure 4, and the candidate implicit-reward measures in Appendix F are retained. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 revises reported Skywork size from 80k to approximately 77k, Unified Feedback size from 800k to approximately 850k, and one training subset from 26k to 27k. Figures 4 and A5 update quantity labels and captions. These are reported setting revisions; the PDFs do not establish that training was rerun.

E4.justification: The early-versus-late token case studies in Figures 5 and A6 are revised, expanding from five to ten examples at each extreme and changing the selected words and rank movements. The data-source/quantity ablations, authority-boost validation, Kendall-tau analysis, and Appendix H trajectory analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the fixed-seed statement, statistical tests and multiple-comparison corrections, standard-error/deviation displays, and Appendix F confidence intervals. Changed F statistics, p-value bounds, and significance markers revise reported outcomes without documenting a new uncertainty-estimation or repeated-run procedure.

E6.justification: Quantitative evidence changes across central analyses. Section 3.1 changes F statistics from 88.8 to 58.3 and 42.3 to 43.2. Tables 1, A2, and A3 replace MWLR scores and token rankings; Table 1's Freedom score changes from 0.55810 to 0.50435, and terminal ranks change from 85,524 to 85,517. Figures 3, 5, and A6 also revise plotted values or examples. The overall agency/communion findings persist.

T1.justification: The RLHF derivation, implicit-reward formulation, MWLR definition, and Appendix F formulas and antisymmetry discussion are unchanged. The KL-divergence notation is restyled without changing the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, five introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims: reward models inherit systematic base-model value biases, these biases appear in implicit rewards, and preference training may attenuate but does not reliably eliminate them.

C2.justification: Section 6 removes v1's explicit limitation that focusing on the first output token precludes inference-time compute. Appendix H also drops the agency-specific qualification when suggesting that Qwen's preference gap widens during training. The principal interpretations and remaining limitations are retained.

D1.justification: The reproducibility statement supplies a separate Generalizable-Reward-Model repository for RM training code and explicitly states that code and data are publicly available. The existing analysis-code and checkpoint locations remain. This improves documented access information; repository contents were not externally checked.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds Murthy et al. (2026) as concurrent work finding persistent base-model effects through RLHF and relates those findings to this paper. Other reference changes primarily concern bibliographic formatting or corrections.

P1.justification: v2 standardizes terminology such as pretrained, Big Two, and MFD2, polishes grammar and cross-references, revises acknowledgments, and shortens one author's displayed name. The main section sequence, contribution structure, and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: The figures undergo broad visual revision, including standardized axes, typography and panel labels, reorganized panels in Figure A2, and expanded token-change bar charts with a new color scheme in Figures 5 and A6. Figure 5 moves from page 8 to page 9. This substantially reworks the visual presentation beyond numerical table updates.

improvement.justification: v2 improves figure labeling and presentation, reconciles several stated data quantities with plotted labels, and provides a specific training-code location. These support a limited gain in clarity and reproducibility. The scientific argument remains substantially unchanged; unexplained numerical replacements and removal of the inference-time-compute caveat limit the improvement.
